top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is an invention (magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms, cancelling the lattice light shift in the Lamb-Dicke regime) with strong experimental verification: several independent laboratories reproduce and compare clocks at the 10^-18 level. It opens a new regime for tests of gravity, constants and dark matter. The two-name allocation to Katori and Ye matches the original proposal and the demonstrated realization, and a citation worded around the lattice mechanism does not repeat the 2005 or 2012 prizes. It is mature and verified, so I prefer it to no award, although I cannot fully settle the priority questions for other contributors.
recusal_note: none apparent for B013 (no known connection to Katori or Ye); B015 electron microscopy is my own field but is not on this slate; shared Chalmers affiliation with Goran Johansson is not relevant to this proposal
